text: Every router here shares one channel. So who gets to talk?
When two transmit together, both get scrambled.
So Wi-Fi listens first, then waits a random number of tiny slots.
Pick the same number? They clash, and each doubles its waiting range.
More neighbours on your channel means more waiting, whatever your internet plan.
Pick a quieter channel, or move to five gigahertz, with far more room.
For private nearby messaging, even offline, try Meshline.
